payload.title: Generalize herdr-spawn executor adapter (src/runner/dispatch/transport.mjs::herdrSpawnAdapter) so…
payload.description:
Generalize herdr-spawn executor adapter (src/runner/dispatch/transport.mjs::herdrSpawnAdapter) so ANY agent CLI (claude, agy, codex, pi) can be launched via a real herdr pane purely by config, achieving two goals simultaneously: (1) live TTY visibility matching each CLI's real streaming behavior, (2) correct synchronous {status,stdout} result returned to the dispatch ladder, with the pane auto-closed once truly done.

Context already researched (see docs/history for this item once created, and the parent conversation):
- herdr-plugin's real launch mechanism (herdr-plugin/src/pick.rs open_pick_pane/run_argv_for_command) types a DIRECT interactive claude --model {model} --dangerously-skip-permissions '<prompt>' command into a pane, fire-and-forget (never waits on stdout/exit code) -- different from herdr-spawn's current synchronous contract (throwaway sh script + sentinel + herdr pane wait-output polling to fabricate an exit code/stdout for executeExecutorCli's synchronous return).
- Claude Code -p text mode BUFFERS (no live output until done, per official headless.md docs); -p DOES exit with a real subprocess exit code; --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages streams live but as JSON-lines needing translation to readable text.
- agy's own -p headless mode ALREADY streams live plain text natively (live-verified in this repo's own docs/history/executor-dispatch-fallback-live-monitor/RESEARCH.md and docs/history/dispatch-cli-execute-progress-visibility/RESEARCH.md) -- no translation needed.
- pi --mode json emits a real AgentSessionEvent JSONL stream (docs/history/pi-executor-runtime-capacity/RESEARCH.md, evidence fixtures under docs/history/pi-executor-runtime-capacity/evidence/*.jsonl) -- needs translation like claude's stream-json.
- codex exec's live-streaming default is UNVERIFIED -- treat as unknown, do not guess.
- Consolidates/supersedes tsk-3d5 (empty placeholder, same stated goal).

Required changes:
1. Fix: herdrSpawnAdapter's success path never closes the pane (only timeout does) -- add herdr pane close <paneId> on success too.
2. Add optional liveOutput: { streamFlags: string[], renderer: string } field to an executor invocation (config.mjs validation + transport.mjs consumption). Present: append streamFlags to args, wrapper script shebang sh->bash (need ${PIPESTATUS[0]}), pipe command through tee <raw-jsonl> | node <renderer>, capture real exit code via PIPESTATUS[0]. Absent: byte-identical to today (no regression).
3. Write two renderer scripts under new src/runner/dispatch/live-renderers/: claude-stream-json.mjs and pi-agent-session.mjs (ground truth: real evidence fixtures in docs/history/pi-executor-runtime-capacity/evidence/).
4. Config changes in .fgos/config.json: rename executors.agy -> executors.agy-cli (grep repo for other agy executor-id references); add executors.agy-herdr (adapter herdr-spawn, no liveOutput, ACTIVE -- wire capabilities.fgos-coding-implement.prefer to it, replacing claude-herdr); add liveOutput to existing executors.claude-herdr but leave dormant/unreferenced; add new executors.pi-herdr (with liveOutput/renderer) and executors.codex-herdr (no liveOutput, unverified) both dormant/unreferenced with description explaining how to activate.
5. Test: extend test/runner/herdr-spawn-adapter.test.mjs for pane-close-on-success and liveOutput/PIPESTATUS pipeline (mocked, no regressions). Required real proof: dispatch one real fgOS work item through executors.agy-herdr against the actually-installed herdr and agy binaries (not mocked) -- confirm live pane visibility, auto-close on completion, correct real status/stdout, and the dispatched item's own fgOS state actually advances. Capture as real, reproducible evidence.

Constraints: preserve herdrSpawnAdapter's existing {status, stdout, paneId} return contract exactly for the no-liveOutput default path. Scope is herdr-spawn generalization + config + renderers + tests + one real live proof -- does not touch herdr-plugin/src/*.rs.

payload.title: Bug: settleClaim's CAS check (src/state/store.mjs:1101-1106, getItemDurableRevision…
payload.description: Bug: settleClaim's CAS check (src/state/store.mjs:1101-1106, getItemDurableRevision src/state/runtime-coordination.mjs:49) compares the item's durable revision hash against preClaimRevision frozen at the ORIGINAL fgos pick/take claim moment -- but any legitimate fgos discover/plan/edit/decision/handoff call between claim and return (the normal path for any item that goes discovery->planning->executing under one continuous claim, per fgos-coding-driving's own design) mutates the item and changes getItemDurableRevision's hash (it hashes the WHOLE item object via JSON.stringify). This makes fgos return fail with 'settleClaim: item durable revision changed from X to Y' even though X->Y is entirely this same session's own legitimate progression, not a concurrent interloper. Reproduced live this session on tsk-5jl: claimed via fgos pick at stage discovery, advanced through fgos discover (->planning) and fgos plan (->executing) plus several fgos edit/decision/handoff calls in between, then fgos return failed twice with the identical 'durable revision changed' error (same from/to values both times, ruling out a genuine concurrent race). No CLI verb exists to refresh a runtime claim's own preClaimRevision after such legitimate intermediate writes (claim-port.mjs exports only claimWork). Workaround used this session: directly patched the gitignored, ephemeral .fgos/runtime/claims/<id>.json file's preClaimRevision field to the current hash (the exact 'to' value the engine's own error already reported), which is safe (never touches the durable events.jsonl) but is a manual, undocumented recovery path a normal caller has no way to discover or perform safely. Needs a real design fix: either (a) preClaimRevision should be narrowed to hash only fields that indicate a genuinely CONCURRENT write this session did not itself make (e.g. exclude fields settleClaim/discover/plan/edit/decision/handoff already know they legitimately touched), or (b) each of those legitimate mutating verbs should refresh the active claim's own preClaimRevision as part of its own write (same critical section), or (c) a resync-claim verb should exist alongside fgos resync-worktree for exactly this recovery, discoverable and documented like docs/how-to/fix-fgos-write-rejected-merge-block.md is for the ADR0020 case. Until fixed, every coding-domain item that goes through discovery/planning stages under one continuous claim (not picked directly at stage executing) risks this same false-conflict at return time.

payload.title: Redesign executors.agy-herdr's completion-detection to use agy's real interactive mode…
payload.description:
Redesign executors.agy-herdr's completion-detection to use agy's real interactive mode (-i/--prompt-interactive) instead of headless -p, so the herdr pane shows agy's real rich TUI (banner, live spinner, box-drawn UI) instead of a plain -p text dump, while still giving herdrSpawnAdapter a correct, deterministic exit code and auto-close -- via an adapter-driven two-phase completion sequence: (1) type 'agy -i {prompt}' directly into the pane (no disposable sh/bash script wrapper at all for this path -- the prompt goes straight to agy as its real initial interactive turn), (2) adapter polls the pane's own live text for a genuine 'model has stopped generating' signal, (3) once detected, adapter sends a SECOND herdr pane run typing '/exit' into the same pane, waits for the shell prompt to return, then sends a THIRD herdr pane run typing 'echo "<sentinel>:\0"' to capture agy's real process exit code, (4) parses that sentinel, closes the pane, returns {status, stdout} exactly like the current sentinel-based path.

Context already researched and empirically verified LIVE this session (not guessed):
- 'agy --help' confirms '-i'/'--prompt-interactive': 'Run an initial prompt interactively and continue the session' -- real flag, already installed (agy 1.1.21).
- Live-tested 'agy -i <prompt>' in a real herdr pane: shows a genuinely rich interactive TUI (banner, model info, live spinner 'Generating...'/'Working...', box-drawn accept-edits status bar, '? for shortcuts' idle indicator) -- confirmed via herdr pane read polling every 1s during a real long-running prompt (multi-second essay generation), content visibly changing between polls (real live activity, not a frozen buffer).

payload.title: Bug: fgos main-checkout-reset's safety guard (assertSafeMainCheckoutReset,…
payload.description:
Bug: fgos main-checkout-reset's safety guard (assertSafeMainCheckoutReset, src/runner/main-checkout-reset-guard.mjs) only checks whether the working tree is DIRTY (uncommitted changes) before allowing 'git reset --hard <sha>' on the shared main checkout (bin/fgos.mjs:4402-4414) -- it never checks whether --sha is behind current HEAD by real, already-COMMITTED commits. When the tree is clean (both sessions had already run a real git commit), the guard permits the reset unconditionally, even without --confirm, silently discarding N real commits with zero ancestor check, zero commit-count warning, zero listing of what is about to be lost.

Real incident, 2026-08-26 ~13:44-13:49 UTC: two concurrent sessions each committed directly to the shared main checkout on top of merge commit 16e9cff4 -- my .fgos/config.json flip (6c5538cb) and another session's src/runner/dispatch/cli.mjs + test/runner/dispatch.test.mjs refactor ('Route fanout-batch dispatch decisions through compileDispatchPlan', 26d16fbd). ~38 seconds after the second commit landed, something reset main back to 16e9cff4 (git reflog: 'reset: moving to 16e9cff4' at 13:49:04 UTC), discarding both commits from main entirely. Both were recoverable only because they were still dangling git objects (git cat-file -t confirmed both alive, not yet gc'd) -- pure luck of timing, not a designed safety net; my commit was recovered via git cherry-pick 6c5538cb (now 1ffc61a0), the other session's 26d16fbd was deliberately left untouched per the user's explicit choice not to touch another session's work without their own context.

The engine's OWN truncation-guard caught a SIDE EFFECT of this on .fgos/events.jsonl -- .fgos/logs/main-checkout-guard-warnings.jsonl logged multiple content-mismatch/regressed entries at 13:55:49 UTC (e.g. 'seq 62 now points at a different event than the last recorded mark ... file: events/58a4960c-2feb-44d3-9acc-34e3bcb0aebe-20260826T101158878Z.jsonl' -- this exact session's own tsk-3vz submit/edit/move events, seq 62-64, permanently lost) -- but nothing caught or prevented the loss of the two real SOURCE commits themselves, and there is no equivalent guard scoped to arbitrary tracked files/commits on the shared main checkout, only to .fgos/events.jsonl specifically.

This is a broader, more severe variant of the already-investigated docs/history/events-jsonl-git-tracked-truncation/ class: that investigation (tsk-cgg) explicitly scoped its own detection (a gitignored high-water-mark sidecar) to reverts of .fgos/events.jsonl specifically, not to detecting/preventing loss of arbitrary tracked source commits on the shared main checkout. tsk-3au's own main-checkout-reset verb was built specifically to prevent 'a session running reset --hard after checking only the 3 files it meant to touch, discarding other in-flight sessions' work' (per the guard file's own header comment) -- but its actual check only defends against UNCOMMITTED work, missing the exact case demonstrated here: two sessions' already-COMMITTED work getting discarded by a reset to a stale/captured sha.

Could not determine from available logs whether the destructive reset was invoked via 'fgos main-checkout-reset --sha 16e9cff4' specifically, or a raw 'git reset --hard 16e9cff4' bypassing fgos entirely (AGENTS.md warns against the latter in prose only, not enforced by any hook) -- the other session's own tool-call transcript was not accessible to this investigation. Either way, the guard as currently implemented would not have blocked either path once the tree was clean.

Suggested direction (not prescriptive -- let discovery/planning judge): assertSafeMainCheckoutReset (or the CLI verb wrapping it, bin/fgos.mjs's main-checkout-reset case) should also check whether sha is a strict ancestor of current HEAD with real intervening commits, and if so, refuse or require an explicit stronger confirmation that lists the commits about to be discarded (author, message, files touched) -- similar in spirit to how git itself warns before a force-push would lose commits. Also worth considering: should a raw git reset --hard on the main checkout be caught by a git hook (not just AGENTS.md prose), given this is the second real incident (after tsk-cgg) of the exact same underlying habit causing real, undetected-until-after-the-fact damage.

payload.title: Bug: executors.agy-herdr's interactiveMode adapter (herdrSpawnInteractiveAdapter,…
payload.description:
Bug: executors.agy-herdr's interactiveMode adapter (herdrSpawnInteractiveAdapter, src/runner/dispatch/transport.mjs:538+) never actually delivers the prompt to agy -- confirmed real dispatch does no work at all, every time.

Root cause: the adapter types ONE command line into the pane -- 'agy -i <prompt> --mode accept-edits --new-project --model <model>' (the full invocation, prompt included as a positional CLI arg, same shape as the -p headless invocation it replaced). Under -p, agy auto-submits that positional prompt as chat input and starts working headlessly. Under -i, it does NOT -- agy just opens its real interactive REPL, shows its idle 'Accept-edits mode' banner, and sits there waiting for a human to type something. Nothing in the adapter ever types the prompt into the pane as a SEPARATE follow-up input (the same way it already does for exitCommand: 'herdr pane run <paneId> /exit'). The adapter's own agent_status polling (checkIdle) then correctly and honestly reports 'idle' -- because agy genuinely is idle, having never received the prompt -- so runExitSequence fires, types /exit, extracts a real exit code (0), and returns 'success' with headBefore==headAfter and stdout containing only the startup banner. This is a SILENT FALSE-SUCCESS on every single interactiveMode dispatch, not a rare flake -- confirmed reproducible on 3 separate real dispatches across 2 sessions (this session's own live-proof test during tsk-3vz/tsk-4zi, a fresh disposable-repo repro just now, and another concurrent session's real work-item dispatch which hit it twice in a row and fell back to claude cli-spawn on its own initiative).

Impact: capabilities.fgos-coding-implement.prefer was flipped to agy-herdr (tsk-3vz/tsk-4zi) then reverted back to agy-cli within the same session once this was found (commit 21966be3) -- so production dispatch is safe again, but any real work items that WERE dispatched through agy-herdr during the brief window it was active (tsk-4kn and possibly others) may have received a false 'success' with zero actual work done and should be re-checked.

Why the earlier tsk-10j/iron-law-evidence.md live tests didn't catch this: those tests used trivial single-line print prompts ('Print Hello from agy-herdr interactive live proof') and asserted only res.status === 0, explicitly deferring stdout-content verification as an accepted best-effort limitation (screen-clear-on-exit) -- so a dispatch that did zero real work but still exited 0 looked identical to a real success under that test's own assertions. The gap was never 'stdout retention is lossy', it was 'the prompt is never delivered at all' -- a much more fundamental defect the existing tests structurally could not distinguish from the accepted limitation.

Suggested direction (not prescriptive): after the pane boots and agy's own agent_status first transitions to a state indicating it's ready for input (or after a fixed settle delay), the adapter should type the prompt itself as a separate 'herdr pane run <paneId> <prompt text>' call -- mirroring how exitCommand is already delivered -- rather than relying on -i to auto-submit a positional CLI argument the way -p does. Needs a real live test asserting actual file/commit output, not just exit code 0, before this is trusted again.
